items.name: SR 26-2
items.description: Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management — Federal Reserve Board, FDIC, OCC (replaces SR 11-7)

requirements.text: Banking organizations are expected to maintain model risk management practices appropriate and effective for the risks they face; the guidance is most relevant to organizations with over $30 billion in total assets and sets no enforceable standards.
requirements.rationale: Sound model governance remains essential for safety and soundness even where the guidance is non-prescriptive.

controls.description: Develop and maintain a written model risk management policy approved by the board of directors.

requirements.text: Model risk management practices should be commensurate with the model risk presented by the organization's models, considering model materiality (exposure and purpose) and the size and complexity of operations.
requirements.rationale: A risk-based, tailored approach ensures governance effort tracks actual model risk rather than applying uniform rigor.

controls.description: Classify models by materiality (inherent risk in the context of exposure and purpose); apply governance rigor commensurate with each tier.

requirements.text: Validation should occur prior to a model's first use, with nature, rigor, and frequency aligned to the model's approach, use, and materiality; its quality depends on the rigor and effectiveness of the review rather than the organizational structure of the validation function.
requirements.rationale: Risk-aligned validation keeps scrutiny proportionate while still characterising model risk and limitations.

controls.description: Maintain a model validation procedure applying effective challenge — objective reviewers with appropriate expertise, sufficient independence for objectivity, and standing to effect change; scale rigor to model materiality.

requirements.text: Validation should include outcomes analysis — comparing model outputs to real-world outcomes (e.g., back-testing or outlier analysis) — to evaluate performance against objectives and business use.
requirements.rationale: Performance assessment ensures models produce reliable outputs and reveals deterioration over time.

controls.description: Implement back-testing procedures comparing model predictions to actual outcomes; document and report results quarterly.

requirements.text: Maintain a model inventory with sufficient information to understand model risks at the individual and aggregate level, with detail tailored to model complexity and overall model usage.
requirements.rationale: An inventory sized to actual usage underpins effective model risk management without mandating a single format.

controls.description: Maintain a central model inventory system tracking all models, their purpose, tier classification, validation status, and last review date.

requirements.text: Before a model is deployed, the organization should confirm that the model functions as intended.

controls.description: Implement pre-deployment checklists verifying data feeds, integration points, user training, and monitoring procedures are all operational.
